decoded.scope-drift: Against p-20260917-atlassian-mcp-unauthenticated (34 scopes, 2026-09-17 18:06Z): four added, read:assets:agent-interface, write:assets:agent-interface, read:jira-align:agent-interface, write:jira-align:agent-interface; none removed; the other four keys unchanged. Compared by parsing both JSON documents, not by counting
decoded.v1-paths: POST initialize to https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp/authv2 answers 401 with resource_metadata for its own v1 document plus error=invalid_token; https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/sse answers 401 Bearer realm="OAuth", error=invalid_token; both bodies 79 bytes, both as on 2026-09-15 (artifact sections 9 and 10)
decoded.ownership: GET /.well-known/public-agents.json on www.atlassian.com answers 404 (the site's HTML not-found page); _public-agents.atlassian.com TXT answers NODATA (Status 0, no Answer section) through a public resolver (sections 11 and 12)

finding: The keyless state of the documented endpoint is unchanged from the 2026-09-15 and 2026-09-17 readings: an initialize request with no credentials answers 401 with an RFC 9728 resource_metadata pointer, and the two v1 paths answer their own 401s. What changed is the advertised scope list of the v2 protected-resource document, which is the vendor's machine-readable statement of how much product surface an agent may hold: 38 scopes today against 34 ten days ago, with Assets and Jira Align added (read and write) and nothing removed. No credential was used, no client registered, nothing written; the server's tool list remains unmeasured.

reproducibility.command: curl -sS -D - -o - -X POST https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp -H 'accept: application/json, text/event-stream' --json '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"plumb-probe","version":"1.0"}}}'; curl -sS https://mcp.atlassian.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v2/mcp
